question: In February 2003, why was a blue curtain hung over the tapestry copy of Guernica at the United Nations?
answer: Officially, to give television cameras a plain backdrop outside the Security Council. It went up as the case for war on Iraq was being made there, and many read it as hiding a picture of a bombed town's civilians at the worst moment. Sixty-six years after Picasso painted it, the image was still too pointed to stand behind.
move: An image people take care to cover is still doing its work.
ask: What truth in my life do I keep covering because it is too uncomfortable to stand next to?
source: Dowd, The New York Times, February 2003
reference: Maureen Dowd, Powell Without Picasso, The New York Times, 5 February 2003
